args.name: Sela Thorn

properties.role: Tide-reader offering passage from pier four to the old chapel; refuses to row at night.
properties.played_as: Whispers as if the water might hear; avoids eye contact and watches the tide line.

sources.quote: Sela Thorn. I read the tides. I'll row you, but not at night. Never at night.
She talks in a whisper, like the water might hear her, and she never once looks you in the eye. She keeps her gaze on the tide line.
Sela, Sella, the dockhands say it both ways.

args.why: Introduces the voiced tide-reader and preserves both spellings as one person.

sources.quote: She shrugs and goes back to her net. She says she'll be at pier four tomorrow at first light if you want the ride.

args.why: Records Sela's last observed location at the docks.

args.name: Sela's offer of passage

properties.what_is_open: Sela offered to row the party to the chapel for two silver and said she would be at pier four tomorrow at first light; passage has not happened.
properties.next_step: Meet Sela at pier four tomorrow at first light.

sources.quote: Fine, she'll do it for two silver.
She shrugs and goes back to her net. She says she'll be at pier four tomorrow at first light if you want the ride.

args.why: Preserves the agreed price and offered meeting as an unresolved arrangement.

sources.quote: Sela Thorn. I read the tides. I'll row you, but not at night. Never at night.

args.why: Identifies the person offering passage.

args.name: Sela's account of Saltmere's flooding

properties.statement: Sela says Saltmere flooded forty years ago on the night the bell first rang, and reports her grandmother saying the water rose warm; the timing is unconfirmed.

sources.quote: Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang. Forty years ago. My grandmother said the water came up warm.

args.why: Records Sela's account and her grandmother's report without establishing the claimed timing as fact.

sources.quote: Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang. Forty years ago. My grandmother said the water came up warm.

args.why: Connects the attributed flooding account to Saltmere.

properties.details_shown: Up the cliff path, closed for forty years. Black entrance in chalk with half-rotted timbers and an overturned rusted cart. Warm air smells of old candle wax. Thirty paces in, warm black water holds wet hymn-book pages against the walls.
properties.state: Closed; tunnel flooded about thirty paces inside.

sources.quote: The Saltmere Mine entrance is a black mouth in the chalk, timber frame half rotted. A rusted cart lies on its side. The air coming out of it is warm and smells like a church, like old candle wax.
About thirty paces in, the tunnel floods. Black water, and it's warm to the touch. Floating on it, stuck to the walls, there are pages. Wet pages from a hymn book.

args.why: Adds what the party directly observed inside the mine.

args.name: Hymn page marked M. Brand at Saltmere

properties.statement: A wet hymn page recovered at Saltmere describes the sea giving back what it takes and bears the pencilled margin inscription "M. Brand".

sources.quote: A hymn about the sea giving back what it takes. And in the margin, in pencil, someone wrote "M. Brand".

args.why: Records the physical clue separately from Teo's identification of its writer.

sources.quote: About thirty paces in, the tunnel floods. Black water, and it's warm to the touch. Floating on it, stuck to the walls, there are pages. Wet pages from a hymn book.
A hymn about the sea giving back what it takes. And in the margin, in pencil, someone wrote "M. Brand".

args.why: Locates the physical clue at Saltmere.

properties.what_changed: A hymn page at Saltmere bears "M. Brand". Teo identifies the handwriting as Mira's and believes she was here; the transcript does not confirm that identification.

sources.quote: A hymn about the sea giving back what it takes. And in the margin, in pencil, someone wrote "M. Brand".
That's Mira. That's my sister's handwriting. She was here.

args.why: Advances Teo's search while preserving his identification as a player interpretation.

args.name: Is Maren involved with the Hollow Choir?

properties.what_is_open: Vessa and Oren suspect Maren is behind the cult or running the choir. The GM did not confirm this.

sources.quote: Okay, I bet the harbor-master is behind all this. Maren wanted us gone from day one. She's in the cult, I'm calling it.
Yeah, Maren is totally running the choir.
You can think that. Roll investigation if you want to search the rest.

args.why: Preserves the players' suspicion as an open question rather than changing Maren's established identity.

properties.details_shown: Sank into the bay with its bell. At low water the bell tower and two broken arches protrude, with seaweed on the stones. At midnight pale shapes stand in rows on the submerged chapel floor like a congregation, then disappear when the bell stops.

sources.quote: The drowned chapel's roof sticks out of the bay at low water, just the bell tower and two broken arches. Seaweed hangs from the stones.
Shapes. Pale shapes, standing on the chapel floor under the water, in rows. Like a congregation. Then the bell stops and they're gone.

args.why: Adds the visible ruins and the witnessed congregation-like shapes.

args.name: Unnamed fisherman at the chapel shore

properties.role: One of two fishermen hauling their boat up below the chapel.
properties.played_as: Warns the party away from the water with the Kelp Mother tale, insisting "Everyone knows that." Leaves with the other fisherman.

sources.quote: Two fishermen hauling their boat up. One of them sees you looking at the water.
Don't stand that close. The Kelp Mother takes children who stand that close. Pulls them down by the ankles. Everyone knows that.
That's what the fishermen say. They pull their boat up and leave.

args.why: Records the voiced fisherman without conflating him with Sela or Bram despite the shared speaker label.

args.name: The fishermen's Kelp Mother warning

properties.what_is_open: A fisherman claims the Kelp Mother pulls children into the water by their ankles. The GM attributes this to fishermen; its truth is unknown.

sources.quote: Don't stand that close. The Kelp Mother takes children who stand that close. Pulls them down by the ankles. Everyone knows that.
That's what the fishermen say. They pull their boat up and leave.

args.why: Keeps the local warning as an unresolved rumor without establishing a creature as real.

sources.quote: Don't stand that close. The Kelp Mother takes children who stand that close. Pulls them down by the ankles. Everyone knows that.

args.why: Preserves who supplied the warning.

sources.quote: (to himself) That's the choir clock at three of six.

args.why: Records the GM's explicit advance from two to three segments; player visibility stays unchanged.

properties.what_is_open: Who or what rings the drowned bell remains unknown. It rang twelve times at midnight; louder humming accompanied pale congregation-like shapes on the submerged chapel floor, which vanished when it stopped.

sources.quote: And then, right at midnight, the bell rings again under the water. Twelve times. And the humming is back, but louder. Much louder than two nights ago. You can feel it in your teeth.
Shapes. Pale shapes, standing on the chapel floor under the water, in rows. Like a congregation. Then the bell stops and they're gone.

args.why: Advances the bell investigation with direct observations while leaving the ringer unresolved.

args.name: The Tarred Gull

properties.details_shown: Tavern by the Gullwick docks; a fire burns and it smells of tar and fish stew.

sources.quote: You end up back at the Tarred Gull, the tavern by the docks. Fire going, it smells of tar and fish stew.

args.why: Records the new location where the party ends the session.

args.name: Bram

properties.played_as: Huge, red-bearded; laughs at his own jokes and wipes the same mug while talking. Calls the party brave or stupid and offers stew on the house.

sources.quote: The innkeeper, Bram, sets down three bowls of stew without being asked.
You lot went to the shore at midnight? Brave or stupid. On the house, either way.
Bram is huge, red beard, laughs at his own jokes, and he wipes the same mug the whole time he talks to you.

args.why: Records the newly voiced innkeeper and his portrayal.

sources.quote: You end up back at the Tarred Gull, the tavern by the docks. Fire going, it smells of tar and fish stew.
The innkeeper, Bram, sets down three bowls of stew without being asked.

args.why: Locates Bram at the inn he runs.

args.name: Bram's account of Maren's brother

properties.statement: Bram says he has known Maren for thirty years, calls her sharp-tongued but good-hearted, and says she lost a brother to the bay; this is his account.

sources.quote: Maren? Thirty years I've known her. Sharp tongue. Good heart. She lost a brother to that bay.

args.why: Preserves Bram's testimony about Maren without treating it as GM-confirmed history or disproving the players' suspicion.

sources.quote: Maren? Thirty years I've known her. Sharp tongue. Good heart. She lost a brother to that bay.

args.why: Connects Bram's attributed account to Maren.

properties.next_step: The party plans to meet Sela at first light tomorrow and dive to the chapel at low tide during the day. Vessa intends to buy rope and a second lantern tonight; purchase and departure are not confirmed.

sources.quote: At low tide, during the day. Not at night, Sela was right about that.
So tomorrow, first light, Sela rows us out and we dive to the chapel at low tide. I'll buy rope and a second lantern tonight.
Agreed. Tomorrow we dive.

args.why: Captures the party's agreed next action without recording it as completed.

properties.what_changed: A hymn page at Saltmere bears "M. Brand"; Teo identifies it as Mira's handwriting, without GM confirmation. Teo believes the hymns came from the chapel and agrees to dive there tomorrow to pursue the lead.

sources.quote: A hymn about the sea giving back what it takes. And in the margin, in pencil, someone wrote "M. Brand".
That's Mira. That's my sister's handwriting. She was here.
Okay, plan. Mira wrote in that hymn book. The chapel is where the hymns came from. We go down to the chapel.
Agreed. Tomorrow we dive.

args.why: Records the clue and Teo's intended pursuit without establishing his deductions as facts.

sources.quote: You end up back at the Tarred Gull, the tavern by the docks. Fire going, it smells of tar and fish stew.
Yes, long rest, you're all back to full. And that's where we stop for tonight.

args.why: Records where the character ends the session.

Yes, long rest, you're all back to full. And that's where we stop for tonight.
